BALTIMORE â€”Some Baltimore housing residents have no heat amid frigid temperatures Tuesday.

Some residents of Gilmor Homes told 11 News that their heat isn't working. They said housing officials gave them space heaters, but those aren't working either.

Tyesha Harrell, a resident of Gilmor Homes and mother of five, received new radiators for heat, but she said they don't work. She said she reported it to housing officials in November.

"They gave me two space heaters and only one of them is working, and we also have to use the oven to warm up. We have to all sleep in a little room, because we only have one space heater, so we have to huddle up together so we can keep warm," Harrell said.

Harrell said a contractor who came out to look at the problem said the pipe inside her unit is bad and they're not sure how to fix it.

Harrell isn't the only resident at Gilmor Homes going through these frigid temperatures with no heat.

"It's pretty cold in my apartment. I (have to) keep a coat on, a jacket on, things of that nature," said Cedric Mayers-Hairston, a resident.

The group Communities United has gotten involved, advocating for more than a dozen residents who they said face the same problem. Perry Hopkins, with Communities United, said they've met with housing officials but haven't seen any real action.

"There has been some cosmetic progress made, but the true issues and needs of this community are still being left unaddressed," Hopkins said.

They're hoping to draw attention to the issue so Harrell and others can live comfortably in their homes or be moved to units where the heat is working.

"Everything needs to be fixed or I need to be out of here. I (have to) be out of here, because it's not safe for me or my kids," Harrell said.

In response, Baltimore Housing spokeswoman Tania Baker told 11 News in a statement, "There were a total of 13 units that reported insufficient heat, 11 have been issued space heaters, two units did not respond to maintenance when they arrived. Maintenance will return to those units before the end of the business day. Staff are working on the system to address the inefficiency issues."
